Thirty kilometres of coast

Event Planners in Northern Beaches

No train reaches the Northern Beaches, which changes every plan made here. Guests drive, catch a bus or come by ferry, and a Sunday afternoon in February can add forty minutes to the trip. Tell us your date and hear from planners who work the peninsula.

There is no train. Everything else here follows from that one fact.

Transfers, parking, supplier travel and where guests sleep all get harder without a railway line. Planners who work this coast solve those four first and design the day around the answers.

The Northern Beaches run roughly thirty kilometres of coast from Manly to Palm Beach, with Pittwater on the western side and bushland behind. It is one of the most beautiful parts of Sydney to hold an event and one of the most awkward to get to, because no railway line has ever been built here. Ask event planners in Northern Beaches postcodes what they sort out first, and most will say transport. Everything downstream depends on it: the ceremony time, the length of the gap, whether you need coaches, and how late the bar can run.

The venue types follow the coast. Surf clubs and headland reserves in the south, waterfront settings along Pittwater at Church Point and Newport, and private properties through Seaforth, Frenchs Forest and Terrey Hills where a marquee becomes an option.

In and around Northern Beaches

What are you planning in Northern Beaches?

Six briefs come up again and again along this coast. What separates them is not budget so much as how far north the venue sits and how many guests have to be moved to it.

Start with

Weddings

Ceremony on a headland or a beach reserve, reception at a surf club above it. That combination is what people come here for, and it carries a permit, a wind contingency and a transport plan. Palm Beach and Avalon weddings also need somewhere for guests to sleep.

Find planners

Parties and milestones

Milestone birthdays here are often at home, because the houses have decks and the views do the decorating. The planning goes into catering that can work out of a domestic kitchen, parking on a street with no footpath, and a finish time the neighbours can live with.

Find planners

Corporate events

Brookvale, Dee Why, Frenchs Forest and Warriewood carry the local business base, and their events tend to be offsites, team days and client functions that use the coast as the drawcard. Expect a hard finish, because staff have to drive home down a peninsula with limited roads.

Find planners

Engagement parties

Late afternoon on a deck at Freshwater, Collaroy or Mona Vale, sixty people, a grazing table and the sun going down behind the houses. Simple to picture and worth planning properly, because the onshore wind gets up around four and the parking runs out before that.

Find planners

Proposals

Barrenjoey headland, the Curl Curl and Dee Why rock pools and the Pittwater foreshore at Church Point are the settings people ask for. All are public, most involve a walk, and the light is best early. A planner scouts access, weather and the exit, then keeps it quiet.

Find planners

Private celebrations

Christenings, wakes, club functions and long lunches fill the smaller rooms from Balgowlah to Narrabeen, usually at short notice. A coordinator brought in for the final fortnight is often all that is needed, mainly to hold the caterer, the hire delivery and the parking to one timeline.

Planning support

How much help do you want in Northern Beaches?

Distance decides this one. An event in Manly or Balgowlah can run on coordination alone because suppliers reach it easily. Anything north of Mona Vale involves travel fees, accommodation and a transport plan, and that is full planning work.

Full planning

A planner carries the whole build with you, from the first budget conversation to the last supplier leaving.

Usually engaged nine to fourteen months out.

You have made a start. A planner picks up the parts that have stalled and brings the rest into one plan.

Your plan is built. A coordinator takes it over in the final weeks and runs the day so you can be in it.

Usually engaged four to eight weeks out.

Venue sourcing

Planners who know a market can shortlist against your date, your numbers and your budget rather than sending you back to the same search results.

Event coordination

Coordination is the execution layer: suppliers confirmed, a run sheet everyone has, and one person answering questions on the day.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Northern Beaches

Four questions separate a planner who has worked up here from one who has only driven through. Every one of them is about getting people and equipment onto the peninsula.

No. 01

Ask what their transport plan costs

Coaches are not an upgrade here, they are usually the answer. Ask a planner to price guest transfers as a line item from the start: how many vehicles, from where, at what times, and whether they wait or return. A planner who has run Palm Beach weddings will quote it without being prompted, because the alternative is fifty cars on a road with nowhere to put them.

No. 02

Ask which suppliers charge travel past Mona Vale

Supplier travel fees are real on this coast and they rise sharply the further north you go. Caterers, hire companies and staffing agencies based on the north shore or in the city commonly add a delivery charge or a minimum spend for the northern end. Ask a planner which of their regular suppliers already work up there without a surcharge.

No. 03

Ask who applies for the reserve permit

Headlands, beach reserves and foreshore parks along this coast are council land, and setting up chairs, an arbour or a signing table needs a booking. Applications take time, numbers are capped and the space stays public. Confirm whether the planner lodges it, when the deadline falls, and what the wet weather alternative is, because the permit does not move with the weather.

No. 04

Ask where the guests sleep

Accommodation thins out north of Newport, and that is a planning problem rather than a guest problem. If half your list is coming from the city, work out early whether they stay in Manly or Dee Why and travel up, or whether you build the night around a single return coach. Deciding late leaves people driving home tired on a dark coast road.

Twenty minutes on a map is an hour on a Sunday in January. Plan for the real number.

On the ground

Getting a hundred guests up a peninsula with no railway

Three facts govern events on this coast: there is no train, the roads narrow as you go north, and the wind arrives most afternoons. Plan against those and the rest is straightforward.

The road is the whole transport system

Traffic here is not background noise, it is a scheduling input. The peninsula narrows to a small number of through roads, and on a summer weekend a twenty minute drive from Manly to Mona Vale can take an hour, longer again if there is surf or a market on. Build the run sheet from the arrival time backwards and add a buffer nobody would add in another part of Sydney. The B-Line bus and the Manly ferry carry a lot of guests, and both are worth naming on the invitation with the actual times on them.

Wind, sand and an exposed coast

The onshore breeze is the most predictable design constraint here. Most afternoons from spring through summer, a steady wind comes off the water from early afternoon onwards, and it will take a lightweight arbour, a stack of menus, a floral installation and the top tier of anything unweighted. Plan for it: weight everything, avoid loose paper, keep the ceremony early or tuck it behind a headland, and have a sheltered position identified before the day. Beach ceremonies also need a hard surface plan for anyone in a wheelchair.

Two different coasts, north and south

The peninsula behaves like two markets, and the dividing line sits somewhere around Mona Vale.

  • South, from Manly to Narrabeen: more venues, more accommodation, ferry and B-Line access, and suppliers who come without a surcharge.
  • North, from Newport to Palm Beach: fewer rooms, thinner accommodation, longer supplier drives and a real case for coaches.
  • West, along Pittwater: Church Point, Bayview and the Scotland Island water access properties, where a boat becomes part of the plan.

Questions

Planning an event in Northern Beaches

How much does a wedding planner cost on the Northern Beaches?

Easy Weddings (updated February 2026) puts on the day coordination at $1,500 to $2,000 and full service planning at $5,000 to $6,000 nationally, and those figures are the right starting point here. What sits on top on this coast is transport and travel: coaches for guests, and supplier delivery fees that climb once your venue is north of Mona Vale. Ask for both to be quoted as separate lines rather than folded into an estimate.

How do guests get to Palm Beach without a train?

By car, by coach or by ferry, and for a large guest list the coach is usually the only sensible answer. There is no railway line anywhere on the Northern Beaches, and Palm Beach sits at the far northern tip, about an hour and a half from the city on a good run and considerably more on a summer Sunday. Parking at the northern reserves fills early. Book transfers when you book the venue.

Do I need a permit for a beach or headland ceremony?

Yes. Beaches, headlands and foreshore reserves from Manly to Palm Beach sit on council land, and any ceremony with chairs, an arbour or a signing table needs a booking through the council before the day. Expect a fee, a cap on guest numbers, a fixed time slot and no exclusive use of the space. Apply early for popular headlands in October to March, and have a wet weather site approved as well.

Will suppliers charge travel to come to the Northern Beaches?

Many will once you are past Mona Vale, and it is worth asking before you shortlist. Caterers, hire companies and staffing agencies based in the city or on the north shore price the northern end of the peninsula as a long round trip, often with a delivery charge, a minimum spend or an overnight rate for a two day build. A planner who works this coast will already know which suppliers do not add one.

What time of year is best for an outdoor event here?

Late March to May and September to early November give the best combination of light, temperature and manageable wind. December to February brings heat, crowds, full car parks and a strong onshore breeze most afternoons. June to August is cold and exposed on the coast, though Pittwater sits more sheltered than the ocean side. If you want a beach ceremony in summer, put it early in the day rather than at four.

Where should out of town guests stay?

Manly and Dee Why hold most of the accommodation, and it thins noticeably north of Newport. If your venue is at Avalon Beach or Palm Beach, decide early whether guests base themselves in the south and travel up by coach, or whether the small number of northern options gets booked out by your group. Either way, put the answer on the invitation, because guests booking late will end up an hour away.
